claims.text: The magnetocaloric response of the specified FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons is governed by an interplay among nanostructure, magnetic properties, and heat-transfer rate.
The hysteresis of the specified FeMnNiGeSi-type nanoscale films or nanoribbons is governed by an interplay among nanostructure, magnetic properties, and heat-transfer rate.
Magnetic softness is a key factor controlling the magnetocaloric behavior and hysteresis of the specified alloy.
Vanishing magnetostriction is a key factor controlling the magnetocaloric behavior and hysteresis of the specified alloy.
Low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles constitute the controlled intervention.
Nanostructure acts as the structural mediator.
Heat-transfer rate limits the achievable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
Low-applied-field cycling will enhance magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Low-applied-field cycling will reduce hysteresis relative to the as-deposited baseline.
A notable bulk magnetocaloric response may be lost in a genuinely low-dimensional state.
The proposed operating regime is low applied field in a genuinely low-dimensional state.
Magnetization and heat-capacity measurements will be used to evaluate magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
The hypothesis is falsified if magnetocaloric response and hysteresis do not decrease by at least 10% relative to the as-deposited state.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome calls for enhanced magnetocaloric response, whereas the falsification rule implicitly expects magnetocaloric response to decrease by at least 10%. These are opposite directional predictions.
